equity_bridge.item: FY2025 final dividend declared (US$0.10/share), in trade and other payables at 30 Jun 2026, paid July 2026
equity_bridge.note: Interim Report 2026 statement of changes in equity, note 12(b); 30 June cash of US$559.3m is pre-payment

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: mid-cycle intra-Asia container volume growth of 3-4% p.a. (Analysis JSON industry outlook) less ongoing rate deflation from the record orderbook; the historical CAGRs are cycle artefacts and were not used
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Revenue 3yr CAGR FY2022-FY2025 is -19.3% (FY2022 was the post-pandemic super-peak, US$2,443m revenue and US$1,075m net income) while the 2yr CAGR from the FY2023 trough is +21.2%; equity compounded at -0.5% p.a. over the same three years only because US$898m of dividends were paid out. Owner FCF was negative in FY2023 and FY2024 (fleet investment plus high lease cash), so no FCF CAGR is computable. Every CAGR here measures where in the freight cycle the endpoints fall, not the business's growth rate.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (treatment B): FY2023 -474.9, FY2024 -178.6, FY2025 +230.3, H1 FY2026 -2.9 (US$ m). Reported FCF on the same periods: -267.5, -62.8, +301.5, +45.3. The gap is interest income plus IFRS-16 lease cash (US$159m in FY2023 when most capacity was chartered in, US$56m in FY2025).

scenario_narratives.base: Mid-cycle reversion. The FY2024-FY2026 margins (37-40% EBITDA ex interest and disposal gains) are Red-Sea-supported peak-cycle numbers and are not extrapolated. Rates deflate through 2027-2028 as the record orderbook delivers, the Group's own ~93,600 TEU of newbuilds (+67% on today's ~140,000 TEU) is absorbed partly by replacing chartered-in tonnage and partly by the new semi long-haul services, and the business settles at a 27% EBITDA margin, ~12% owner-FCF margin and a ~9% return on today's book equity. The valuation lands below book value: at mid-cycle rates the committed US$1.15bn fleet program returns less than the 10.5% cost of capital.
scenario_narratives.bull: Disruption-supported rates persist (Red Sea, Hormuz, tariff-driven rerouting), China+1 keeps intra-Asia volumes compounding at 5-6%, and the diversification into Middle East, Mexico and Red Sea lanes lifts revenue per TEU. Margins hold around 30% and recover to 32% as the owned fleet reaches full utilisation; the zero-debt balance sheet lets the Group keep paying ~US$0.17/share of dividends through the build-out.
scenario_narratives.bear: Overcapacity cycle. Durable Suez normalisation coincides with peak newbuild deliveries, rates return to FY2023 levels, and T.S. Lines - a sub-scale regional carrier with no structural moat - takes the price cut while still funding US$858m of committed capex from cash. Owner FCF is negative for two years, the dividend is cut, and the business recovers only to a 21% mid-cycle margin. Equity value is then mostly the cash and the young fleet at a cyclical-trough multiple.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A zero-debt, cash-rich, young-fleet intra-Asia carrier valued on mid-cycle owner cash flow rather than on the Red-Sea-boosted margins of the last three years. Leases are an operating cost, interest income is stripped because the cash is added back, the newbuild program is charged in full as it falls due, and the terminal value is capped at a cyclical multiple. The trailing 6-9x P/E and ~10% dividend yield the market shows are peak-earnings artefacts; the question that matters is what the fleet earns when freight rates normalise.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mid-cycle margin judgment (27% base) is the dominant driver: each 1pp of terminal EBITDA margin is worth roughly US$0.08-0.10/share (HK$0.6-0.8)
Timing and scale of newbuild capex: the FY2027-28 outflows are modelled from the US$857.7m commitment; slippage into 2029 or vessel resales would shift value forward
Red Sea / Suez normalisation and the pace of orderbook deliveries determine whether FY2027 looks like the base (+1% revenue) or the bear (-8%)
Tax: shipping income is currently exempt; a Pillar Two or Taiwan/HK regime change toward a 15% rate would cut terminal FCF by ~12%
USD/HKD peg: per-share HKD values assume the 7.75-7.85 band holds
Leadership transition to the second generation (June 2026) and the family's Wan Hai relationships are relationship-based rather than structural advantages

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API for 2510.HK at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range HK$7.46-14.96. USD/HKD from Yahoo HKD=X on the same date.
data_sources.financials: 2510.HK_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, millions USD); Annual Report 2025 (cash flow statement lines 2986-3045, note 4 other revenue, note 5(c) depreciation split, note 15(b) lease cash); Interim Report 2026 (balance sheet, cash flow statement, capital commitment US$857.7m, interim dividend US$0.070/share, no dilutive instruments); Annual Report 2024 for FY2023 lease cash and ROU depreciation comparatives.
data_sources.qualitative: 2510.HK_Analysis.json (2026-10-18): business model, fleet program, orderbook and Red Sea risk, management's cautious H2 FY2026 commentary.

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E container-shipping revenue: H1 FY2026 actual US$660.4m + H2 at +3% YoY (US$662.6m), i.e. the H1 run-rate. FY2025 actual was US$1,284.8m. Charter-hire revenue from vessels chartered out (US$96.8m FY2025) and container rental income sit in 'other revenue' below this line and are carried inside the EBITDA margin, not the revenue base.
inputs.share_count_basis: 1,665,031,000 shares in issue (Interim Report 2026, share capital note 12(a); unchanged since the Nov-2024 IPO). No share options or awards outstanding - basic and diluted EPS are identical (US$0.140 H1 FY2026). Held flat; SBC is nil.
inputs.net_debt_note: Zero bank borrowings (nil gearing). Lease liabilities of US$167.0m (62.1 current + 104.9 non-current at 30 Jun 2026) are EXCLUDED from net debt because the lease cash cost is charged inside the flows (treatment B). The US$166.5m FY2025 final dividend that sat in payables at 30 June and was paid in July 2026 is deducted via equity_bridge. The US$116.6m interim dividend (US$0.07/share, paid 23 Oct 2026) is assumed to be funded by H2 FY2026 owner FCF (~US$110m: H2 EBITDA ~US$220m less ~US$20m lease cash, ~US$90m capex and nil tax), so the 30 June cash less the final dividend is taken as the year-end FY2026 net cash the FY2027+ flows build on.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2025 owner FCF = reported FCF 301.452 (OCF 502.145 - capex 200.693) - SBC 0 - bank interest income 14.854 - lease principal 53.243 - lease interest 3.067 = 230.288. Owner-FCF history on the same basis: FY2023 -474.9 (reported -267.5, interest 48.4, lease 159.0), FY2024 -178.6 (reported -62.8, interest 21.7, lease 94.1), FY2025 +230.3, H1 FY2026 -2.9 (reported 45.3, interest 6.6, lease 41.6; US$63.6m vessel-disposal proceeds excluded). The series is dominated by the fleet build-out, which is why the forward build runs from components rather than from this base.
inputs.sbc_source: Cash flow statements FY2023-FY2025 and Interim Report 2026: no share-based payment line, no equity-settled awards, no option scheme disclosed. SBC-zero market; rows kept explicit at 0%.
inputs.fx_note: USD/HKD 7.8479 (Yahoo HKD=X, 2026-10-16). Statements are expressed in US dollars; the HKEX quote is HKD. Per-share values are computed in USD and multiplied by 7.8479. No dual listing exists for a parity check; the HKD peg band (7.75-7.85) bounds the rate and the company itself used US$1:HK$7.8 to translate the interim dividend (US$0.070 = HK$0.546), a 0.6% difference.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-16T08:08:14Z regular close (HKEX Friday close; valuation written Sunday 2026-10-18)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Flows are USD, so the rate is built in USD: 10-year UST ~4.2% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~1.25 for a sub-scale container carrier = ~10.5% cost of equity; with zero debt WACC = cost of equity = 10.5%. One rate across all three scenarios - cyclicality and the orderbook risk are priced in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the discount rate (adaptations rule f).
inputs.lease_treatment: B - leases as operating cost. IFRS 16 lease cash (principal, in financing: US$53.2m FY2025, US$38.7m H1 FY2026; interest: US$3.1m / US$2.9m) is charged inside EBIT through lease_cost_pct_path (5.0% of revenue in FY2027, easing to 4.0% as newbuilds replace chartered-in tonnage; FY2025 actual 4.4%, H1 FY2026 annualised 6.3% after new container and vessel charters lifted lease liabilities to US$167m). Lease liabilities are therefore excluded from net debt, and da_pct_path is depreciation EX right-of-use assets (FY2025 US$100.8m = 7.8% of revenue; H1 FY2026 US$44.0m = 6.7% annualised; ROU depreciation of US$55.4m / US$33.6m is NOT in the D&A path so the lease is charged once).
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are immaterial (US$0.1m of equity, US$84k of H1 FY2026 profit); flows are taken as 100% attributable and no NCI deduction is made in the bridge.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical') with the adaptations file applied - USD-built WACC, single lease treatment, SBC-zero, excluded-income/matching-asset rule (bank interest income stripped from the flows because the US$559m cash pile is added back in the bridge). EBITDA margin paths are post-IFRS-16 reported EBITDA (which includes charter-out and container-rental income) EXCLUDING bank interest income and vessel-disposal gains: on that basis FY2023 14.6% (trough), FY2024 38.9%, FY2025 36.8%, H1 FY2026 40.4% (US$312.7m less US$39.4m disposal gain less US$6.6m interest), FY2026E ~36-37% assuming a softer H2. The build deliberately does not extrapolate the FY2024-FY2026 Red-Sea-supported margins: the base reverts to a 27% mid-cycle EBITDA margin (roughly the midpoint of the FY2023 trough and the current peak, lifted slightly for the structural shift from chartered-in to owned tonnage, which moves cost from charter hire to depreciation). Capex follows the disclosed newbuild program: US$857.7m committed at 30 Jun 2026 (13 vessels, ~93,600 TEU, delivering 2026-2028) on top of US$289.9m already prepaid, so FY2027 and FY2028 capex are 33% and 28% of revenue before falling to a ~10.5% renewal rate, held equal to ex-ROU D&A in the terminal years so the terminal FCF does not rely on under-depreciating a young fleet. Cash tax is ~0 today (international shipping income is exempt in Hong Kong and excluded from Pillar Two GloBE; FY2025 cash tax was a US$0.6m refund) and is ramped to 3% of EBIT as a prudence margin. Working capital capture is 0: payables exceed receivables so growth is roughly cash-neutral. Asset cross-check: book equity is US$2,187m = US$1.31 = HK$10.3/share, with a ~5-year-old fleet carried at or below market (H1 FY2026 disposals realised a US$39.4m gain on US$24m of book); the base DCF below book says the committed newbuild program earns less than the 10.5% WACC at mid-cycle freight rates, which is the central judgment of this valuation.
inputs.price_note: Last regular HKEX close; not an after-hours print. 52-week range HK$7.46-14.96.

bear.narrative: Suez reopens durably while the ~13m TEU orderbook (38% of the fleet) delivers through 2028: freight rates fall back toward FY2023 levels, revenue drops 8% then 4% despite more capacity, and the EBITDA margin troughs at 16% in FY2028 (FY2023 actual was 14.6%) before recovering to a 21% mid-cycle as a sub-scale carrier with no pricing power. The US$858m newbuild commitment is still paid (35%/32% of a smaller revenue base), so FY2027-28 owner FCF is deeply negative and consumes roughly US$550m of the cash pile. Terminal cap 10x.

base.narrative: FY2027 revenue +1%: ~10% more deployed capacity as the 5,300 and 14,000 TEU newbuilds deliver, offset by high-single-digit rate deflation as the industry orderbook lands and Red Sea diversions partly unwind. Margin falls from ~37% (FY2026E) to 30% in FY2027 and bottoms at 24% in FY2029 before settling at a 27% mid-cycle level as the owned fleet lowers charter costs. Capex 33%/28% of revenue in FY2027-28 covers the US$858m commitments, then a 10.5% renewal rate equal to ex-ROU D&A. Terminal multiple capped at 12x owner FCF for a cyclical.

bull.narrative: Red Sea/Middle East disruption persists and absorbs the new tonnage; China+1 relocation keeps intra-Asia and Indian-subcontinent volumes growing 5-6%; the Middle East, Mexico and Red Sea services scale at above-fleet-average revenue per TEU. Margin eases only to 29-30% and recovers to 32% as the young owned fleet reaches full utilisation. Same capex program; cap 14x for a business that has proven it can earn mid-teens ROE through a cycle.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 30% from the 15% house default: the Analysis JSON rates freight-rate cyclicality, orderbook overcapacity, trade-policy risk and geopolitical lane disruption all 'high', the industry is at or near a margin peak, and the company is committing US$858m of capex into that supply wave. Bull cut to 20% because it needs two independent things to hold at once - continued geopolitical disruption absorbing capacity AND rate discipline among larger competitors - and management itself guided cautiously for H2 FY2026. Base 50%.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
